display.purpose: The hero sentence only, set as four clipped line boxes that rise on load; columns 1 to 8.

headline.purpose: Project titles on a spread and section headings, always on a 5-column block; a Project title is a link in ink that turns narra on hover.

mail.purpose: The Contact email line in narra with a 2px underline.

title.purpose: The role name in an Experience row.

lede.purpose: The role and availability sentence under the hero, capped at 34ch.

body.purpose: Spread prose and Experience descriptions; the only serif text on the page.

action.purpose: Buttons and the Open the Case Study link.

ui.purpose: Masthead brand and links, table cells, organisation lines, the Contact side note.

meta.purpose: The Work / Private / Case Study line, Experience dates, the footer.

caption.purpose: The Evidence line and plate captions; the archipelago caption runs one step smaller (0.75rem, 1.4) in Ink 3.

label.purpose: Uppercase table column heads only; the Credential tag reuses the size at weight 400. Never above a heading.

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: The only easing curve; exponential ease-out for every transition and keyframe.

motion.name: hero-rise
motion.value: 900ms, translateY(110%) to 0 inside clipped line boxes; stagger 60ms / 150ms / 240ms / 330ms
motion.purpose: The four lines of the hero sentence on load.

motion.name: hero-below
motion.purpose: The lede and buttons after the sentence.

motion.name: scan
motion.value: 1500ms sweep from top to the map's height, 80ms delay; 1900ms on the pulse
motion.purpose: A 2px ink scan line across the archipelago on load and on each pulse.

motion.name: dot-pop
motion.value: opacity 480ms, scale 0.2 to 1 in 640ms, delay calc(row * 22ms + 120ms)
motion.purpose: Dots appear behind the scan line, north to south.

motion.name: pulse
motion.value: every 7000ms from 2600ms; per dot 1400ms fill to ink and back, delay row * 28ms
motion.purpose: A slow signal pulse while the map is at least 20% in view and the tab is visible.

motion.name: pointer-signal
motion.value: fill 300ms to narra, scale 1.5 in 640ms, no delay; radius 36 map units
motion.purpose: Dots near the pointer light in narra and reset on leave.

motion.name: button-wipe
motion.value: ::before scaleX 0 to 1 from the left in 320ms; colour and border 200ms
motion.purpose: Button hover wipes to ink; no lift, no press.

motion.name: arrow-slide
motion.purpose: The Case Study link's arrow on hover.

motion.name: row-tint
motion.purpose: Stack index rows tint to a 45% capiz wash on hover.

motion.name: link-underline
motion.purpose: Links darken their underline from 50% narra to narra on hover.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: prefers-reduced-motion: reduce settles every transition and animation instantly and disables smooth scrolling
motion.purpose: ?motion=off and data-theme are review-only overrides, not product features.

breakpoints.name: wide-hero
breakpoints.purpose: Hero sentence takes the full width; the archipelago moves below it on columns 7 to 12.

breakpoints.name: narrow
breakpoints.purpose: Spread blocks, section headings and content lists go full width in source order.

breakpoints.name: compact
breakpoints.purpose: Hero is a single column; archipelago caps at 300px; hero buttons stack full width.

breakpoints.name: phone-nav
breakpoints.purpose: The Stack index table becomes stacked rows.

breakpoints.name: phone
breakpoints.purpose: Experience rows stack the date above the role.

theme.note: The prototype's data-theme attribute and ?motion=off query are review-only overrides, not product features.

fonts.loading: Google Fonts in the prototype; the production Next.js build should self-host both families.

production.note: Tokens are mapped onto shadcn's CSS variables with --radius: 0; shadcn's default look (Geist, zinc, rounded cards, dark dashboard) is never used.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The one filled narra action per viewport (Email). Hover wipes to ink from the left in 320ms; square, no lift.

components.css: .ds-plate { margin: 0; max-width: 640px; font-family: 'Familjen Grotesk', 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif; } .ds-plate-frame { background: var(--plate, #EDEBE5); background-image: radial-gradient(var(--plate-dot, #CFCAC0) 1px, transparent 1.2px); background-size: 18px 18px; background-position: 9px 9px; padding: clamp(20px, 3vw, 36px); border: 1px solid var(--rule, #C4BFB2); } .ds-plate svg { width: 100%; height: auto; display: block; } .ds-plate figcaption { font-size: 0.8125rem; color: var(--ink-2, #5C5750); margin-top: 12px; line-height: 1.45; display: grid; grid-template-columns: auto 1fr; gap: 12px; } .ds-plate figcaption b { color: var(--ink, #1E1C19); font-weight: 600; white-space: nowrap; } .ds-p-line { stroke: var(--ink-2, #5C5750); fill: none; stroke-width: 1.25; vector-effect: non-scaling-stroke; } .ds-p-box { stroke: var(--ink, #1E1C19); fill: var(--plate, #EDEBE5); stroke-width: 1.25; vector-effect: non-scaling-stroke; } .ds-p-box.ds-hi { fill: var(--green, #1F3A2E); stroke: var(--green, #1F3A2E); } .ds-p-text { font-family: 'Familjen Grotesk', 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 11.5px; font-weight: 500; fill: var(--ink, #1E1C19); } .ds-p-text.ds-on { fill: var(--capiz, #FBFAF6); } .ds-p-small { font-family: 'Familjen Grotesk', 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 10px; fill: var(--ink-2, #5C5750); } .ds-p-arrow { fill: var(--ink-2, #5C5750); }

components.name: Evidence Line and Case Study Link
components.description: How a spread's prose ends: an Evidence line in caption type over a hairline, then the narra Case Study link whose arrow slides 6px on hover.
components.html:
A grading method that scores every telco on six pillars, and an AI pipeline that turns the scores into the monthly report, formatted and ready to sign.

Evidence: internal deployment, write-up only. The full method and a demo on Illustrative Data are in the Case Study.

Open the Case Study

components.css: .ds-map { position: relative; width: 240px; margin: 0; padding: 12px 0 0; font-family: 'Familjen Grotesk', 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif; } .ds-map-frame { position: relative; } .ds-map svg { width: 100%; height: auto; display: block; } .ds-dot { fill: var(--green-2, #4F7A63); opacity: 0.55; transform-box: fill-box; transform-origin: center; transition: fill 300ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), transform 640ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); } .ds-dot.ds-w1 { fill: var(--green, #1F3A2E); opacity: 0.8; } .ds-dot.ds-w2 { fill: var(--green, #1F3A2E); opacity: 1; } .ds-map:hover .ds-dot { animation: ds-pulse 1400ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) calc(var(--r) * 28ms) 1; } @keyframes ds-pulse { 0% { fill: var(--green-2, #4F7A63); } 18% { fill: var(--ink, #1E1C19); } 100% { fill: var(--green-2, #4F7A63); } } .ds-scan { position: absolute; left: 0; right: 0; top: 0; height: 2px; background: linear-gradient(90deg, transparent, var(--ink, #1E1C19) 30%, var(--ink, #1E1C19) 70%, transparent); opacity: 0; pointer-events: none; } .ds-map:hover .ds-scan { animation: ds-scan 1900ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) 1; } @keyframes ds-scan { 0% { transform: translateY(0); opacity: 0; } 8% { opacity: 0.9; } 90% { opacity: 0.6; } 100% { transform: translateY(339px); opacity: 0; } } .ds-map figcaption { margin-top: 18px; font-size: 0.75rem; color: var(--ink-3, #8A847A); line-height: 1.4; max-width: 34ch; } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-map:hover .ds-dot, .ds-map:hover .ds-scan { animation: none; } }

narrative.northStarStatus: proposed; derived from the Tropical Modernist direction notes and PRODUCT.md, not yet confirmed by Robin
narrative.overview:
The site is built the way a Philippine mid-century building is built: a capiz-white ground, poured concrete-gray fields for the rooms that matter (the hero, the Stack index, Contact), narra wood on the one thing a Visitor is meant to touch, and a deep green that carries every datum. Each Project is an editorial spread, not a card: a large title, a short prose block that ends in an "Evidence:" line, and a diagram plate drawn on drafting-dot paper with a hairline frame and a "Plate n" caption. Spreads alternate text-left / plate-right and plate-left / text-right on a 12-column grid, so the page reads like a well-set journal rather than a feed.

The signature object is the dot archipelago: authored island polygons rasterised to a 34 by 48 grid, set bare on the concrete with one caption beneath, scanned in from north to south on load and pulsing slowly while the hero is on screen. It returns as a 26px mini map at the right of the footer, with no words beside it. The Filipino identity lives in the materials (capiz, concrete, narra) and in the archipelago; nothing is labelled as Filipino, and nothing is decorated as such. Motion is one authored moment on load plus quiet control feedback; the rest of the page is still.

Confirmed visual rejections (from the brief): Inter on near-black, purple gradients, glassmorphism, bento stat grids, typewriter titles, skill bars, logo walls, emoji headers, the Brittany Chiang navy/spotlight look, and any Filipino kitsch (Baybayin, flag colours, jeepneys, sun-and-stars). Voice, proposed: plain, specific, first person, no hype.
keyCharacteristics: Editorial spread per Project: title, prose with an "Evidence:" line, and a numbered diagram plate.
Asymmetric 12-column grid; spreads alternate sides, headings sit on 5 columns and content on 6, with a gutter column between.
Capiz ground, full-bleed concrete fields, narra for links and the primary action only, green for data.
Familjen Grotesk 600 at tight tracking for everything that names or operates; Literata for prose.
Hairline rules, tonal fields and one framed plate instead of cards, shadows or glass.
The bare dot archipelago as the signature object, repeated as a mini map in the footer.
One authored motion moment on load; light by default, dark follows the system, no toggle.

rules.name: The Narra Once Rule
rules.body: Narra appears once per viewport as a filled surface, on the single primary action (Email). Everywhere else narra is a link, a status dot, a focus ring or a pointer highlight, never a background, never a heading, never decoration.

rules.name: The Green Carries Data Rule
rules.body: Green is for values: archipelago dots, the focal node and filled shapes in a diagram plate, the Credential tag. It never colours prose, a heading or a button.

rules.name: The Three Fields Rule
rules.body: Concrete is poured under exactly three rooms: the hero, the Stack index and Contact. Fields are full-bleed sections, not boxes; the ground shows between them. The plate paper exists only inside a diagram plate's hairline frame.

rules.name: The System Theme Rule
rules.body: Light by default; dark follows prefers-color-scheme: dark; there is no toggle. The prototype's data-theme attribute and ?motion=off query are review-only overrides and are not product features.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Familjen Grotesk names and operates; Literata reads. Anything in a heading, button, label, caption, table or nav is the grotesk; running prose is the serif. No third face, no monospace.

rules.name: The Semibold Rule
rules.body: Every heading is weight 600 with negative tracking; the rest of the grotesk runs at 400 and the serif at 400. There is no 700 anywhere and no light weight.

rules.name: The No Kicker Rule
rules.body: Headings stand alone. Uppercase labels exist only as column heads inside the Stack index table and inside the Credential tag; they never sit above a heading as an eyebrow or kicker.

rules.name: The Alternating Spread Rule
rules.body: Consecutive spreads mirror each other. Title and prose share one side; the plate takes the other; the sides swap on every spread so the eye crosses the page as it scrolls.

rules.name: The Empty Column Rule
rules.body: Two halves of a spread never touch. A full column is left empty between them (column 6 on a normal spread, column 7 on an alternate one) so the gap reads as white space, not as a card edge.

rules.name: The Level Legend Rule
rules.body: The masthead is the single sticky element on the page. Nothing else pins, floats or follows the scroll.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Structure is drawn with 1px rules and full-bleed tonal fields, never with boxes. If a boundary needs more than a hairline, it is a section, not a card.

rules.name: The One Elevation Rule
rules.body: Elevation is declared once: the diagram plate is the only framed object, and it lifts by paper and hairline, not by shadow.

dos: Do lay every Project out as a spread: Headline title over Body prose ending in an "Evidence:" line on one side, a numbered diagram plate spanning both rows on the other; alternate sides on each spread (The Alternating Spread Rule).
Do keep a full empty column between the two halves of a spread and let the ground show there (The Empty Column Rule).
Do pour concrete under exactly three rooms (hero, Stack index, Contact) as full-bleed fields, never as boxes (The Three Fields Rule).
Do use narra exactly once per viewport as a filled surface, on the primary action, and otherwise only for links, the status dot, focus and the pointer highlight (The Narra Once Rule).
Do give green to data only: archipelago dots, the focal node and filled shapes in a plate, the Credential tag (The Green Carries Data Rule).
Do set every heading in Familjen Grotesk at 600 with -0.035em tracking, and running prose in Literata.
Do draw every diagram as inline SVG on a plate: drafting-dot paper, 1px hairline frame, "Plate n" caption saying it was redrawn; never a screenshot.
Do keep the dot archipelago bare, as built, with the caption stating that dot weight is illustrative, and repeat it alone as the footer mini map.
Do keep the masthead sticky (brand plus four links, nothing more) and everything else in the flow.

Do keep motion to the one load moment (hero rise, archipelago scan, slow pulse) plus control feedback, all on `cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)`, and settle everything instantly under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
Do let the theme follow `prefers-color-scheme`, light by default, with no toggle; self-host Familjen Grotesk and Literata in the production build.
Do build on shadcn/ui primitives with these tokens mapped onto shadcn's variables and `--radius: 0`.
donts: Don't set Inter on near-black, or reach for the Brittany Chiang navy/spotlight look; its structure may be borrowed, its look may not.
Don't use purple gradients, glassmorphism, blur, gradient text, or any gradient as a surface.
Don't build bento stat grids, skill bars, logo walls, typewriter titles or emoji headers.
Don't use Baybayin, flag colours, jeepneys, sun-and-stars motifs or any Filipino kitsch; identity lives in the materials and the archipelago.
Don't put a kicker or eyebrow above a heading; uppercase labels belong only in table heads and the Credential tag.
Don't use cards as page structure; the diagram plate is the only framed object, and it lives inside a spread.
Don't add box-shadows, a second elevation model, or a radius on any surface or control.
Don't fill a button, heading or background with narra beyond the one primary action, and don't put green on prose or buttons.
Don't add a stat row to a spread, the hero or anywhere else; a number belongs in prose or on a plate, with a Project fact behind it.
Don't animate anything beyond the load moment and control feedback; no scroll-driven effects, no parallax, no hover lifts.
Don't ship shadcn's default look (Geist, zinc, rounded cards, dark dashboard), Google Fonts, a theme toggle, or the prototype's `data-theme` / `?motion=off` overrides and floating review bar.
Don't introduce a third typeface, a monospace, a 700 weight or a light weight.
